messages:
Eva S.: FYI escalated from Mike L. Customer hitting embeddings API dimension mismatch after a migration to their v2 client. Pasting customer payload and server error. Repro steps below.

Mike L.: Customer says error: "embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1536, got 768" when calling /v1/embeddings

Eva S.: here's the curl they used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"text-embedding-1536","input":[["How to reduce latency?"]], "batch_size": 8}'
```

Ken W.: ah that double bracket around the string. They wrapped the input in an extra list so the server thinks they're sending a precomputed vector? The embeddings endpoint treats array of strings vs array of arrays differently and if it sees numbers it tries to validate dims. Does the customer actually send tokens or precomputed floats?

Eva S.: customer pasted full JSON from their Python client:
```json
{"model":"text-embedding-1536","input":np.array(["How to reduce latency?"]).tolist()}
```

Ken W.: looks like their numpy usage led to nested list: when a numpy scalar or 1D array gets converted it can produce extra nesting depending on dtype. Also some HTTP libs wrap single items as [[...]] when doing batch retries. Repro steps I tried locally:
1) send `{"input":"single string"}` -> accepted (we coerce to list)
2) send `{"input":["string1","string2"]}` -> accepted
3) send `{"input":[["string1"]]}` -> server rejects with "expected embedding dim 1536" because our type inference thought they're sending numeric arrays; extra nesting triggers code path for numeric embeddings which then validates length

Mike L.: customer says it started after they upgraded to requests 3.x + a new wrapper. They're batching and using a helper that always wraps into an outer list. So single-item batches become double-wrapped.

Eva S.: Customer wants quick fix. What to suggest?

Ken W.: Short-term: tell them to ensure `input` is a flat list of strings. Example Python snippet:
```py
# correct
payload = {"model":"text-embedding-1536", "input": [text]}
resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, headers=headers)

# avoid doing this
payload = {"model":"text-embedding-1536", "input": [[text]]}
```
If they're using numpy, do `input = list(np_array.flatten())` or `input = np_array.astype(object).tolist()`

Eva S.: Also advised: set batch_size=1 as a temporary measure and upgrade to our client v0.9.3 which normalizes input shapes.

Ken W.: I'll open an internal ticket to improve the error message to call out "unexpected nested list — ensure input is a flat list of strings" and add an extra schema validation in front of the numeric-embedding code path.

eng-bot: Created issue #INF-4823 for "Improve embeddings input shape validation" assigned to Ken W.

Mike L.: Customer confirmed workaround worked after flattening. Will close the support case once we get the server change. :thumbsup:

Eva S.: copying notes to the case: flattened input fix, workaround batch_size, client update, internal ticket INF-4823. Closing here when INF-4823 merged.
